newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa slips by close, volume paltry.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa slips by close, volume paltry.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures drifted within a tight band on Wednesday and prices ended slightly lower in subdued trade, lacking market-moving news, traders said.
"The market is absolutely dead," said a trader.
"There's no feature, prices moved in a narrow seven stg range on December...absolutely there's no business and really I've done nothing," the trader said.
Volume fell sharply to 1,403 lots from Tuesday's 2,200 lots as operators retreated to the sidelines awaiting new supply/demand news.
By the finish, second-position December gave up two stg to 979 stg a tonne, just below the previous minor 980 support.
Technical analysts said the contract, showing more downside risk rather than the upside, now looked set to test the next support at 970.
The prompt September contract also showed signs of weakening, traders said.
"September is weakening. There's more grading going on all the time," said one.
Sept/Dec spread saw offers at 28 stg after trading at 21 stg. "This reflects the fact that there's too much cocoa around, keeping the whole market weak," the trader said.
"The nearbys have been damaged further by the buffer stock manager's sale yesterday," he said.
The International Cocoa Organization's buffer stock manager on Tuesday announced sales of 4,250 tonnes of stockpiled cocoa.
The sale, part of the on-going buffer stock liquidation, was normally seen as routine but traders said the disposal tended to weigh on sentiment especially in a quiet day.
On the fundamental front, Malaysia's major cocoa planter Golden Hope Plantations said it would quit cocoa growing by June 1999 due to prolonged weak cocoa prices.
Elsewhere, the U.S. Commerce Department said cocoa bean imports rose to 29,437 tonnes in July from 20,970 in June and 19,418 in July last year.
